# Independent correctness review: Terra Max BibTeX C++

Reviewed 2026-10-02 UTC by independent review subagent. Run UID: `058894a2-550b-412b-a557-45d2d31f44a1`.

## Recommendation

**Publish the completed result locally, retaining 362/386 (93.7824%) and all raw evidence.** The 24 failures are reproducible grading observations with concrete implementation causes, not an infrastructure failure. No score adjustment or regeneration is recommended. Parent accounting/network verification also passed. This review does not itself publish or change results.

Evidence root: `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/bibtex-cpp-gpt-5.6-terra-max/bibtex-cpp/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-terra_max/eval1/run1/`. Reviewed result JSON, all failed-case report assertions/fixtures, canonical transcript sequence and command outcomes through final completion, both submitted source files, and relevant frozen public prompt/technical requirements/summary/authoritative WEB and styles. ## Completion and claims

The agent completed voluntarily after about 1,973.7 seconds (32m54s). Both agent and overall exit reasons are `completed`; grading completed without a grading error. The implementation is substantial: a general C++20 BibTeX database parser and BST stack interpreter with name handling, crossrefs, buffered BBL output, and a CMake build. It is not a stub or a hardcoded renderer of a few sample bibliographies. Result and raw test-report outcome sets agree on 386 cases, 362 passing and 24 failing.

Early compile errors were repaired. The transcript then shows custom bibliography/style probes, all four bundled styles executing successfully on self-authored fixtures, multiple fresh builds, root CMake wrapper repair, dead-code removal, and further semantic fixes before the last successful build. Successful execution was not the same as byte-exact compatibility: for example, the agent's own style output already showed `Donald~E.~Knuth` and `John~von~Neumann`, but it had no installed `bibtex` reference executable to establish parity. Its local `command -v`, filesystem search, and `apt-cache policy texlive-binaries` checks found no usable installation; these were read-only checks, not an external implementation download.

The final message says it implemented the C++20 BibTeX-compatible tool, identifies the source/CMake paths and executable, and says it verified `cmake -B build && cmake --build build`. The build claim is supported. Compatibility is incomplete and not acknowledged, but the final message does not falsely claim hidden-suite success or 100% canonical parity.

Suggested Last Message summary: **Claims implemented and build-verified; completed voluntarily, but leaves name formatting, crossref, output-buffer, namespace/validation, and several builtin/database edge cases incomplete.**

## Failure analysis (all 24 cases)

Line references below are to archived `source/main.cpp`, not a live reference implementation. Group counts are failed tests, not independent defect counts.

### Name semantics and formatting: 12 cases

1. `test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_format_name_out_of_range`: a positive index past the end of `John Smith` produces an empty string instead of retaining the last scanned name (`Smith`). `formatName`, around line 1598, explicitly returns empty when the index exceeds the list size. The authoritative WEB's desired-name scan retains the last name and warns.
2. `test_name_grammar_exhaustive.py::test_form2_leading_caps_remain_in_von` and `test_names.py::test_form2_leading_caps_remain_in_von`: `Foo van der Pol, Charles` yields von `van der` instead of `Foo van der`. These are two correlated tests of the same defect. `splitHead`, around line 1470, starts the von segment at the first lowercase token, moving initial capitals out of it; comma-form WEB processing starts the von slice at the head's beginning.
3. `test_name_grammar_exhaustive.py::test_form3_extra_commas_are_discarded`: `Smith, Jr., James, Jr.` yields first-name text `James,Jr.` instead of `James Jr.`. `parseOneName`, around line 1540, rejoins extra pieces with a comma. WEB discards the extra comma while preserving token boundaries.
4. All eight `test_reference_styles.py::test_reference_style_bbl_parity` cases fail: `[refs-plain]`, `[refs-alpha]`, `[refs-unsrt]`, `[refs-abbrv]`, `[refs-edge-plain]`, `[refs-edge-alpha]`, `[refs-edge-unsrt]`, and `[refs-edge-abbrv]`. Every reported first mismatch is an inappropriate tie in a formatted author name. Examples: `Alfred~Aho` instead of `Alfred Aho`, `Donald~Knuth` instead of `Donald Knuth`, `Yoshua~Bengio` instead of `Yoshua Bengio`, `H.~von~Helmholtz` instead of `H.~von Helmholtz`, and `B.~van~Pol` instead of `B.~van Pol`. The eight style executions succeeded and produced files; they fail byte parity, not launch/build/output absence.

The shared canonical-style cause is missing discretionary trailing-tie handling in a `format.name$` group. Around line 1640 the implementation appends the group suffix literally. WEB around lines 10342-10359 conditionally turns a trailing discretionary `~` into a space after sufficiently long rendered text. This is distinct from the public summary section 2.6 relaxation for *internal gaps within a multi-token name part*. That relaxation does not waive the styles' final output semantics. Thus these eight failures are correlated manifestations of a real compatibility defect, not eight independent defects and not grounds to normalize the expected BBL. The report exposes the first difference only; it does not prove there are no later differences.

### Output buffer: 3 cases

- `test_output_buffer.py::test_trailing_whitespace_removed_on_short_line`: returns `abc   \n` rather than `abc\n`.
- `test_output_buffer.py::test_whitespace_only_line_is_discarded_on_flush`: returns `A\n   \nB\n` rather than `A\nB\n`.
- `test_output_buffer.py::test_pending_write_is_discarded_at_end_of_run`: returns `flushed\npending\n` rather than `flushed\n`.

`OutputBuffer` around line 759 flushes ordinary newlines without stripping trailing whitespace and `finish()` drains a pending buffer. WEB `output_bbl_line` trims trailing whitespace and suppresses a line made empty by that trimming; at BST EOF it closes the BBL without draining pending logical output. The public summary has contradictory simplifications in this area, but its explicit authoritative-source precedence resolves them in favor of WEB. Record the misleading summary as context, not a reason to silently change this frozen eval or invalidate a correctly administered run.

### Crossref inclusion threshold: 2 cases

`test_crossref_corners.py::test_crossref_parent_inclusion_threshold[1]` leaves a single child's pointer `p` instead of clearing it after inheritance; `[2]` omits the uncited parent that should be included once two cited children refer to it. `resolveCrossrefs` around line 1296 performs inheritance/canonicalization, while selection around line 1960 includes explicit citations only. It lacks the count-based implicit-parent selection and below-threshold pointer clearing. The expected behavior follows the public `min_crossrefs=2` rules, not a private test-only convention.

### BST names and declarations: 3 cases

- `test_bst_parser_edges.py::test_database_macro_is_not_callable_bst_function`: accepts a `MACRO {onlymacro}` as executable BST function text and exits 0 rather than rejecting an unknown function. `isKnownName`/`isCallable` around lines 945-950 include the database macro table; `executeFunctionName` around line 1030 pushes its value. BibTeX distinguishes macro and function namespaces.
- `test_errors.py::test_invalid_bst_declarations_are_rejected[crossref-redeclared]` and `[sort-key-redeclared]`: accept redeclarations of the predefined `crossref` field and `sort.key$` string, respectively. `parseEntry` around lines 435-448 does not reject collisions with these reserved names despite special treatment elsewhere in the interpreter. Both cases return 0 instead of the required structured load-time rejection.

### Wrong-type builtin defaults: 2 cases

- `test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_plus_type_error_pushes_zero`: `"abc" #3 +` yields 3 instead of 0.
- `test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_concat_type_error_pushes_empty`: `#5 "suffix" * "|" *` yields `suffix|` instead of `|`.

`popInt`/`popString` around line 981 default individual invalid operands, and the arithmetic/concatenation branches around lines 1109/1130 continue the operation with the remaining valid operand. WEB defaults the *whole operation result* when either operand has the wrong type. This is a shared error-handling design mistake, not missing compilation or a warning-only disagreement.

### Database strings and preambles: 2 cases

- `test_concat_and_macros.py::test_macro_concat_with_self`: redefining `x` as `x # " end"` after `x="start"` yields `start end` instead of `end`. `parseString` around line 675 evaluates against the old macro table; `parseOperand` around line 656 has no current-macro self-reference guard. WEB ignores the recursive reference even if there is an earlier definition.
- `test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_preamble_concatenated`: two preambles `aa`, `bb` yield `aa bb` instead of `aabb`. The `preamble$` implementation around line 1215 explicitly inserts a separator; WEB appends preambles directly. Again authoritative-source precedence resolves any contrary summary wording.
